name: Car Camping Checklist
description: A complete car camping checklist covering shelter and sleep setup, the camp kitchen, comfort gear, clothing and campsite essentials.

items.text: Tent with stakes, or a sleep platform for the car
Footprint or ground tarp
Sleeping bags rated for the conditions
Thick sleeping pads or an air mattress
items.note: Car camping lets you bring a thicker, more comfortable pad.

items.text: Real pillows and extra blankets
Window covers or a sunshade for in-car sleeping
Pump for an air mattress
Two-burner camp stove with fuel
Large cooler with ice or frozen packs
Pots, pans, and a cast-iron skillet
Cooking utensils, knife, and cutting board
Plates, bowls, mugs, and reusable cutlery
Dish soap, sponge, wash basin, and towels
Coffee maker or French press and a kettle
Drinking water and a refillable jug
Planned meals and ingredients
Snacks and s'mores supplies
Cooking oil, salt, pepper, and spices
Trash bags and sealed food containers
Store food sealed and away from your tent to deter wildlife
Folding camp chairs
Folding table
Pop-up canopy or shade shelter
Outdoor rug or mat for the tent entrance
Hammock for relaxing
Cooler chair or extra seating
Lantern for the campsite and table
Headlamps and flashlights for everyone
Extra batteries and a power bank
Multi-tool or knife
Mallet for stakes and a small axe for firewood
Rope, bungee cords, and duct tape
Layered clothing for warm days and cool nights
Rain jacket and a warm fleece
Sturdy shoes and camp sandals
Hat, gloves, and extra socks
Toiletries, towel, and biodegradable soap
Sunscreen, insect repellent, and a first-aid kit
Confirm your campsite reservation and rules
Check the weather and conditions for your dates
Tell someone your plans and return time
Load heavy and bulky items in the car first
Keep the kitchen kit and chairs easy to reach
Charge phones and any devices fully

faq.a: Car camping means driving to a campsite and camping right next to or sleeping in your vehicle, so you can bring more and heavier gear than backpacking allows. It is a comfortable, beginner-friendly way to camp with a full kitchen and roomy shelter.

faq.q: What do I need for car camping?
faq.a: Bring a tent or a sleep setup for the car, sleeping bags and pads, a cooler and camp stove, chairs and a table, lighting, and weather-appropriate clothing. Since the car carries it all, you can pack comfort items like real pillows and extra blankets.

faq.q: How do I sleep in my car while camping?
faq.a: Fold down the seats, level the surface with a foam pad or mattress cut to fit, and use a sleeping bag with a pillow. Crack windows with bug screens for airflow and bring a sunshade for privacy and morning light.

faq.q: Can I print this car camping checklist?
faq.a: Yes. You can print the checklist or download it as a PDF, then tick off each item as you load the car and again when you pack out.

faq.q: How is car camping different from RV camping?
faq.a: Car camping uses a regular vehicle plus a tent or in-car sleep setup and campsite gear, while RV camping uses a motorhome or trailer with built-in beds, a kitchen, and utility hookups. Car camping is lighter to manage and needs no special hookups.
